brief.headline: Tech leads narrow rally; ASML earnings in six days, gold breaks down
brief.regime_summary: SPY sits 1.65% above its 50-DMA and 8.15% above its 200-DMA, up 1.91% on the week. Realized vol is contained at 10.3% and VIX at 15.77 barely clears its 20-DMA of 15.72. That combination looks benign, but breadth is not: only 3 of 11 sectors trade above their 50-DMAs. XLK is the lone strong sector at +7.3% 20-day momentum. Financials, real estate and materials are the weakest. The tape is risk-on for mega-cap tech and risk-off almost everywhere else. Until breadth widens, breakouts in cyclicals and commodities should be treated with skepticism.

portfolio.note: Up 3.3% on the week, 4.6% above its 20-DMA, RSI 68.2. Earnings are October 28, six trading days away. ATR is 2.15%, so a one-ATR stop sits near $518. Trim risk or define it before the print.

Earnings October 14, six calendar days out. Price is 3.7% below the 20-day high of $1,873.50 and trailing P/E of 58.6 is 49% above its historical median. Only one analyst revised up vs. one down in the last 30 days. Earnings gap risk is high given ATR of 2.74%.

XLE cost basis $88, current price $63.36, down 28%. Sector 20-day momentum is negative at -2.4% and XLE lags the market by 4.6% over 20 days. Bounced 3% this week but is 3.7% below its 20-day high; no fundamental catalyst yet visible.

GLD fell 1.3% this week, now 3.5% below its 20-DMA and 6.9% below its 20-day high. RSI is 36.9 and 20-day momentum is -6.8%. Gold futures (GC=F) confirm: down 3.0% from 20-DMA and RSI 35.4. The trend has shifted; the thesis for holding a commodity position that is now underperforming the market by 9% over 20 days deserves review.

watchlist.name: Micron Technology
watchlist.thesis: MU has the most compelling fundamental revision in the screen. EPS estimates rose 140% and revenue estimates rose 112% versus the September 17 baseline, with 5 upward revisions vs. 1 downward in the last 30 days. Forward P/E is 5.3x. Price is 5.4% above its 20-DMA and only 1.9% from its 20-day high of $1,108.72, with above-average relative volume at 1.19x. Earnings are December 23, so there is runway to develop.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA $1,032.65, 20-day high $1,108.72, ATR-based stop ~$1,042 (1 ATR below current price)
watchlist.risk: Sentiment-driven names with 140% estimate revisions can snap back hard if macro tone shifts to risk-off; thin breadth outside tech amplifies that.

watchlist.name: Shopify
watchlist.thesis: SHOP surged 12% last week and is 16.4% above its 20-DMA at $142.66. RSI is 71.2, near overbought. Seven analysts revised EPS up in the last 30 days with zero revisions down. Trailing P/E of 112 is 6% below its historical median, so valuation is not stretched by its own history. Earnings November 3 is the key event to monitor.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA $142.66, 20-day high $166.96, ATR-based stop ~$159 (1 ATR of $6.68 below price)
watchlist.risk: Price is already 16% extended from its 20-DMA in a tape where only XLK leads; a risk-off shift could compress the multiple quickly at 112x trailing earnings.

watchlist.name: Advanced Micro Devices
watchlist.thesis: AMD is up 5.6% on the week, 9.9% above its 20-DMA, and RSI is 70.7. EPS growth estimate for the current year is 82% and estimates are trending up. The 40-day momentum of 36.2% is the strongest in the screen. Earnings are November 3; the setup is intact but extended.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA $587, 20-day high $659, ATR-based stop ~$622 (1 ATR of $23.43 below price)
watchlist.risk: RSI above 70 and 9.9% gap above 20-DMA in a narrow market means any macro shock could trigger a fast reversion; trailing P/E is 165x.

watchlist.name: CrowdStrike
watchlist.thesis: CRWD scores highest in the screen at 1.74. 20-day momentum is 27.7% and the stock leads its sector by 20.4%. Price is 5.5% above its 20-DMA with RSI at 61, less stretched than AMD or SHOP. Earnings are December 1, giving time for the setup to mature.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA $251.5, 20-day high $287, ATR-based stop ~$254 (1 ATR of $11.49 below price)
watchlist.risk: Daily vol is 59% annualized; a single adverse data point on cybersecurity spending or a sector rotation out of XLK would punish this name disproportionately.

watchlist.name: Novo Nordisk
watchlist.thesis: NVO is 14.6% below its 20-day high, bearish MA stack across 20/40/100-DMAs, and RSI is 34.7. EPS estimates were cut 3.1% in 30 days. The company guides for negative EPS growth this year (-2.2%) and next (-1.9%). The P/E of 9.35x sits 2.3x above its historical median on a price-to-earnings-history basis, suggesting the stock is not as cheap as the raw multiple implies. Earnings November 4.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA $39.95, 20-day high $44.82, ATR-based stop ~$39.27 (1 ATR above entry for shorts)
watchlist.risk: Any positive GLP-1 pipeline readout or competitor setback could produce a sharp bounce; RSI near oversold at 34.7 means mean reversion risk is elevated.

watchlist.name: Oracle
watchlist.thesis: ORCL is in a bearish MA stack and 13.5% below its 20-day high. 20-day momentum is -11.2% and it lags the sector by 18.5% over 20 days. Despite the move down, trailing P/E of 22.5x remains 41% below its historical median, so buyers may look for stabilization. Earnings are December 10.
watchlist.levels: 20-DMA $143.37, 20-day high $165.9, ATR-based stop ~$149 (1 ATR of $6.31 above price for shorts)
watchlist.risk: A bounce in XLK or a positive pre-announcement could close the 13.5% gap to the 20-day high quickly; the stock is already down sharply so short risk/reward narrows.

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.note: Gold fell 1.3% this week and sits 3.0% below its 20-DMA with RSI at 35.4. Two-month momentum is -7.1%; the trend has shifted from bullish to mixed. Watch the 100-DMA for a potential support test.

commodities.name: Natural gas
commodities.note: Natural gas surged 10% on the week, 8.2% above its 20-DMA with RSI at 65. Two-month momentum is +16.4% and it is the only energy commodity showing positive market relative strength. Liquidity is thin; gaps can be wide.

commodities.name: Brent crude
commodities.note: Brent rose 2.4% this week and is 1.3% above its 20-DMA, RSI 58. The 40-day momentum of +17.7% contrasts with WTI's weaker -9.9% 20-day read; the spread is worth monitoring. Thin liquidity flag applies.

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.note: Copper gained 2.3% on the week and is essentially at its 20-DMA. RSI is 53.9 and 20-day momentum is +2.6%, a modest constructive signal consistent with stabilization rather than a trend move. Volume is elevated relative to recent history.

commodities.name: Silver
commodities.note: Silver dropped 2.8% this week, 5.9% below its 20-DMA with RSI at 35.9, consistent with the gold weakness. Relative volume spiked to 16x the average, suggesting a possible capitulation flush; worth watching for stabilization.

risks: ASML reports October 14. The stock is 49% above its historical median P/E with ATR of 2.74%; a guidance miss or order-book softness could move it 5-8% on the day and pressure the broader semiconductor tape.
